description: A Core primitive `right` called as `RIGHT` with too few arguments raises ol-not-enough-inputs whose params.callable is the primitive's canonical identity `right`, not the call site casing — a primitive has no declared spelling, so its identity is the profile's canonical name (lowercased, or the Core canonical for a Heritage alias), exactly what the checker reports; case-insensitive identifiers can never make the call spelling the diagnostic identity, so check() and execute() agree (spec/error-model.md:255-260). Issue #1005. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists and still runs — under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — and is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why only one report survives and it reads `stage: "semantic"`.
